verdict.rationale: Keycloak lets a developer register their own application as an OAuth/OIDC client, issue tokens via standard endpoints (authorization, token, introspection, revocation, dynamic client registration), and supports client-credentials/service-account flows so the app itself can act as an OAuth provider issuing tokens to third-party clients. Realms, client registration, well-known config, and token endpoints are all documented with concrete steps. missing for 10: no independent/hands-on corroboration specifically about acting as a third-party-facing provider (vs. securing one's own app), and no explicit walkthrough of onboarding external third-party clients as consumers.
